items.title: Hundreds protest US Ebola quarantine facility in Kenya

featured_image.name: Protesters demonstrate the Ebola treatment center established or Americans in Kenya

items.description:
Hundreds of young people took to the streets of Nanyuki, Kenya, on Monday to protest the establishment of a U.S. Ebola quarantine facility at the nearby Laikipia Air Base, days after a Kenyan High Court ordered the project halted pending judicial review.[1][2][3]

The demonstrations in the central Kenyan town came as public anger intensified over the Trump administration's plan to send Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya rather than repatriating them for treatment on U.S. soil. Protesters constructed barricades and demanded the facility be shut down by June 9, protest leader Patrick Wahome told Reuters.[2][3]

items.title: Takaichi urges Iran to restore free passage through Hormuz

featured_image.name: Japan PM Takaichi Urges Passage of Vessels Through Hormuz in Call With Iran  - Bloomberg

items.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday called on Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian to demonstrate flexibility in Tehran's negotiations with the United States and to swiftly restore free passage through the Strait of Hormuz for vessels of all nations, according to Japan's Foreign Ministry.[1][2]

items.title: Russia launches major strike on Kyiv, setting apartment buildings ablaze

featured_image.name: Ukrainian capital Kyiv under attack from Russian drones, missiles,  officials say

items.description: A large-scale Russian aerial assault struck Ukraine's capital early on Tuesday, June 2, setting residential buildings on fire and forcing thousands of residents into metro stations and shelters, as Moscow follows through on its threat to conduct "systematic strikes" on Kyiv.

items.title: Frederiksen secures third term as Denmark's PM with new centre-left coalition

featured_image.name: DENMARK-ROYALS-SUMMER TOUR

items.description: Denmark's Social Democratic leader Mette Frederiksen announced on Monday that she has agreed to form a centre-left coalition government, ending more than two months of political uncertainty following the country's March 24 snap election. The deal secures Frederiksen's third consecutive term as prime minister and positions her to continue navigating a diplomatic standoff with U.S. President Donald Trump over the future of Greenland.[1][2][3]

items.title: EU climate chief says COP summits falling short of science

featured_image.name: Climate summits are falling short of what the planet needs, EU climate  chief says | Reuters

items.description:
European Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said on Monday that the outcomes of most recent United Nations COP climate summits have fallen short of the ambitious action scientists say is needed to tackle climate change, according to Reuters.[1][2]

The remarks, made in Brussels, come one week before the start of the Bonn Climate Change Conference (SB64), scheduled from June 8 to 18 in Germany, which is seen as a critical juncture for the multilateral climate system to demonstrate it can deliver on commitments made at COP30 in Belém last November.[3][4]

items.title: Iran cuts off U.S. talks, vows to fully block Hormuz

featured_image.name: TOPSHOT-IRAN-US-ISRAEL-WAR

items.description: Iran suspended negotiations with the United States and declared its intent to completely shut down the Strait of Hormuz, dramatically escalating a months-long standoff that has already pushed global oil inventories to record-low territory and raised the specter of crude prices surging past $150 per barrel.

items.title: Anthropic confidentially files for IPO after $965B valuation

featured_image.name: Anthropic IPO 2026: Why Claude Mythos Has Investors ...

items.description: Anthropic announced Monday that it has confidentially submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, taking its first formal step toward a potential initial public offering of its common stock. The filing positions the Claude AI maker ahead of rival OpenAI in the race to go public among the trio of mega-IPOs expected this year.[1][2][3]

items.title: Anthropic files for IPO after $965B valuation

featured_image.name: Anthropic's Valuation Jumped to Nearly $1 Trillion. Here's ...

items.description:
Anthropic announced on Monday that it has confidentially submitted a draft Form S-1 registration statement to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, advancing one of the most anticipated public offerings in technology history. The filing follows the AI company's $65 billion Series H funding round, closed on May 28, which valued the Claude maker at $965 billion — eclipsing rival OpenAI's last reported valuation of $852 billion.[1][2]

The company did not disclose the size, pricing, or timing of any potential offering, stating that the IPO would depend on market and other conditions. Industry observers expect a listing as soon as this fall, which would make Anthropic the third in a trio of mega-IPOs reshaping public markets in 2026, alongside SpaceX and OpenAI.[3][4]

items.title: Armenia's Pashinyan rejects Russia's call for EU referendum

featured_image.name: Armenia hosts a historic European Union summit as the country charts a  course away from Russia

items.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin called Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan on Sunday to congratulate him on his 51st birthday, a gesture of diplomatic courtesy that contrasted sharply with the escalating pressure Moscow has placed on Yerevan in recent weeks over its pursuit of closer ties with the European Union.

items.title: Iran halts US talks over Israel's escalation in Lebanon

featured_image.name: Lebanese start fleeing south Beirut after Israel says will target the area

items.description: Iran announced on Monday that it would suspend indirect negotiations and message exchanges with the United States through mediators, citing Israel's intensified military operations in Lebanon as a violation of ceasefire conditions. The move threatens to upend weeks of fragile diplomacy aimed at ending the broader conflict between Washington and Tehran.

items.title: Nvidia unveils RTX Spark, its first Windows PC chip in over a decade

featured_image.name: Nvidia's Jensen Huang kicks off Computex 2024 with a spotlight on GenAI and  an accelerated GPU roadmap | TechSpot

items.description: Nvidia officially unveiled the RTX Spark at its GTC Taipei keynote on Sunday evening, marking the company's first consumer Windows PC processor in over a decade and a direct challenge to Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm in the laptop market.

items.title: Kuwait intercepts Iranian missiles as US-Iran strikes escalate near Hormuz

featured_image.name: Centcom: Iran strikes on Kuwait violate ceasefire

items.description: The United States and Iran exchanged fresh military strikes over the weekend, with Kuwait caught in the crossfire early Monday after Iranian missiles and drones targeted a US air base on its territory, marking another volatile chapter in the three-month-old conflict even as both sides signal a desire to negotiate.

items.title: CERN finds high-significance hint of physics beyond the Standard Model

featured_image.name: The exotic particles that could finally break the standard ...

items.description: Physicists working at CERN's Large Hadron Collider have found what may be one of the strongest hints yet that the Standard Model of particle physics is incomplete, publishing results that show rare "penguin" decays of subatomic particles behaving in ways current theory cannot explain. The discovery arrives as the LHC prepares to shut down for its High-Luminosity upgrade — a project now clouded by the United Kingdom's decision to pull funding.

items.title: US and Iran exchange strikes as Trump pushes tougher deal terms

featured_image.name: Trump vows at news conference to obliterate Iran's power plants and bridges  if there's no deal on ending the war

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared early Monday that Iran "really wants to make a deal" with the United States, posting on Truth Social even as both countries exchanged fresh military strikes near the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend — the latest escalation in a three-month-old conflict that continues to complicate diplomatic efforts.[1][2][3]

U.S. Central Command said it struck Iranian military sites along the coast in response to "provocative Iranian actions, including the downing of a U.S. MQ-1 drone operating in international waters." Iran's Revolutionary Guards responded on Monday by claiming a retaliatory strike on a U.S. base, according to Reuters.[2][3]

items.title: France seizes sanctioned Russian tanker in Atlantic

featured_image.name: France intercepts 'shadow fleet' tanker in Mediterranean

items.description: The French Navy boarded and detained the sanctioned oil tanker Tagor on Sunday, May 31, in international waters of the Atlantic Ocean, in the latest Western crackdown on Russia's so-called shadow fleet used to evade energy export restrictions.

items.title: France detains 780 after deadly riots follow PSG's Champions League win

featured_image.name: Paris police detain dozens after violence erupts during celebrations of PSG's  Champions League title

items.description: Paris Saint-Germain's second consecutive Champions League title — sealed in a dramatic penalty shootout against Arsenal in Budapest on Saturday — triggered one of the most violent nights of football-related disorder France has seen, with 780 people arrested and one person found dead on the Paris ring road.

items.title: Iran's Pezeshkian reportedly resigns, citing IRGC takeover

featured_image.name: Pezeshkian: Iran with a different face?

items.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has reportedly submitted a formal letter of resignation to the office of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, claiming he has been systematically excluded from key decision-making and that hardline factions within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps have seized control of government affairs, according to Iran International, which cited an anonymous Iranian official. Iranian authorities quickly denied the report.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Taiwan vows not to be 'silenced' after China expels NYT reporter

featured_image.name: China Expelled Reporter Over NYT Interview With Taiwan President

items.description: Taiwan's Presidential Office on Sunday condemned China's expulsion of New York Times correspondent Vivian Wang, declaring the island democracy "will not be silenced because of oppression" and vowing to continue engaging with international media despite Beijing's pressure campaign against foreign journalists.[1][2]

items.title: Hegseth warns U.S. ready to resume strikes on Iran if talks fail

featured_image.name: Watch: US defence chief Pete Hegseth speaks at Shangri-La Dialogue in  Singapore - CNA

items.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned Saturday that the United States is fully prepared to restart military operations against Iran if ongoing ceasefire negotiations collapse, delivering a pointed message at the Shangri-La Dialogue security forum in Singapore as tensions in the region escalated with a fresh Iranian missile strike on a base housing American personnel.

items.title: Israel seizes Beaufort Castle in deepest Lebanon incursion in 25 years

featured_image.name: Israeli troops have captured the strategic Crusader-built Beaufort Castle  in southern Lebanon, the military announces, as the IDF further expands its  ground offensive against Hezbollah. The IDF says that it launched a

items.description: Israeli forces have captured the medieval Beaufort Castle and pushed past the Litani River into southern Lebanon, marking the country's deepest ground incursion into its northern neighbor in more than 25 years. The advance, confirmed by the Israeli military on Sunday, has shattered a fragile ceasefire and drawn sweeping evacuation orders covering much of southern Lebanon.
